title: How Harvey Graph Helps Deliver More Accurate Legal Work
format_note: Narrated slide-style research explainer: animated data graphics on a light ground, bookended by a dark title card, with burned-in captions of the voiceover.
one_thing: A knowledge graph over legal documents lets the same agent answer with fewer turns and about half the cost per criterion met.

on_screen_lines.text: This video covers an experiment on Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark.
Legal work depends on how documents relate to one another.
For example, a lawyer may need to know which case overruled another, which contract replaced an earlier version, or which side letters belong…
We evaluated the Harvey Graph on synthetic document sets from Legal Agent Bench, which stand in for real firm data.
Edges record how two nodes relate: a draft is a version of an executed agreement, or an amendment changes a covenant.
Every fact also stores a verbatim quote from its source document.
Every most-favored-nation clause in the file can then be found with one query.
To measure what the graph changes, we ran tasks from Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark in eleven use cases, with three agent models.
It finished in fewer than half the turns, and its answer met most of the criteria.
The chart shows the agent's cost per rubric criterion met; on aggregate, count and M&A diligence questions, it fell by close to half.
This has been an overview of the Harvey Graph vision and its impact on agent quality and efficiency.
